control.name: Controls
control.intro: Controls set the ranges and the items of a screen, and download its data. They draw only the control, with no card head or frame, so you can put them anywhere, such as a filter bar above the charts or a page header. They fill the width of their slot and are as tall as the control itself. Their background is left empty, so pick `theme` to match the background they sit on (`dark` on a dark one), and write the name screen readers read in `label`. When the value changes, the card sends a `vzb-change` event (`detail: { name, value }`), and the current value is also written on the card as `data-vzb-value`. Listen for the event and change the text of the JSON inside a chart card, and that card draws again with the new data. The selected span and the thumbs are drawn in the text color so they do not compete with the data colors of the charts.

warning-bars.when: Bars for each period stand against one horizontal line, the same limit for every period, and only the parts above the line blink red. Use it for a trend with the same limit each period, such as a monthly budget or a monthly capacity. Do not use it for a target, where more is better.
rules: Write the periods in `labels`, their values in `values` (the same length) and one limit for every period in `limit`. Write `null` for a period with no value: its slot stays empty, since leaving the period out would shift the time axis. The line is named by `limitLabel` (Limit when empty), written above it with its value. One horizontal line means you only compare bar tops with the line to see which periods went over.

Below the line the bars are gray; only the part above it is red. The card writes the excess above each bar that went over (left out when the slot is too narrow), and on the line below how many periods went over and the total excess. Keeping color for the excess makes what needs attention come first. For a rate (`pct`) the total is left out.

Use it only for limits that should not be crossed. On a target where more is better, the periods that met it would blink red like a warning. If each period has a different limit, one line cannot compare them, so do not use this card.

When the card comes into view the line is already drawn, the bars rise one by one from the left, then only the parts above the line blink three times and stop. No bar is drawn before it rises. The still frame alone shows which periods went over and by how much. Replay it with the button at the top right; when the data changes and the card redraws, the last frame is drawn at once. A monthly trend shows 13 months.

share-waffle.when: A card that draws shares as a 100-cell waffle and flips, one by one, the cells that changed hands since the earlier period. Use it to show how much one item's share grew or shrank, such as a market share or a sales mix. It draws the change between two periods only.
rules: List 2 to 4 items in `items`, each with the raw values (units sold, sales and so on) of the `periods` (the earlier one, then the later one) in `values`. The card computes the shares and the change in points. Each period's cells add up to 100 by giving the leftover cells to the largest remainders (one cell is 1%). With a single period in `periods`, the card draws that period's cells with no period switch. When filtering leaves no item, give an empty `items` array for an empty card.

Name the item to point at in `focus` (empty means the first item). Only that item takes the first data color; the others are gray steps, from dark to light in the order listed. With color on one item only, the cells it gained or lost stand out first. There are three gray steps, so with five items or more, fold the small ones into Others.

Cells fill from the top left, column by column, starting with the focus item (a column of 5 cells is 5%). So when its share grows or shrinks, the cells flip at the end of its block, and a bracket under them gives the change in points. The big number is the focus item's share, and the badge color follows `better` (up · down).

The cells sit right under the big number and grow as large as the space left within the 2-unit height and the width allows. With an inner width of 520px or more, the legend stands in a column to the right of the cells; narrower, it goes below them. With 20 cells across, a wider slot means larger cells, so the flips are easier to see.

With two periods, a period switch sits at the top right of the head. When the card comes into view, the earlier period's cells sit still, then the switch moves to the later period and only the changed cells flip one after another, while the big number and the legend shares follow the visible cells one point at a time. When all have flipped, the bracket and the badge appear and the card stops. The still frame alone shows the current share and how far it moved. Click the switch or use the left and right arrow keys to go back and forth between the two periods (going back, the cells flip in reverse, last flipped first); the switch tells which period the big number and the legend show, so the earlier values are always one step away. When the data changes and the card redraws, it draws the picked period's still frame at once. Hover a cell, or focus the chart and press the left and right arrow keys, to see that item's share (one decimal) and raw value for the period on screen, plus the change in points against the earlier period when the later one is on screen.

rank-lines.when: A card that ranks the items in every period, joins the ranks with S-curves, and plays through the periods one at a time so the moments the order changes are visible. Use it to show how products, channels or branches moved up and down over a year, above all how far one item climbed. Ranks hide the size of the differences, so when the gaps matter, use a line chart.
rules: Put the period names in `labels` and 2 to 8 items in `items`, each with the value of every period (units sold and so on) in `values`. The card ranks each period from the largest value (`better: down` makes the smallest value rank 1). Ties follow the previous period's rank, then the listed order, and a null value takes the item out of that period's ranking and breaks its line. Draw 13 months for a monthly trend.

Name the item to follow in `focus` (empty means the first item). Only that item takes the first data color; the rest stay gray, so one path can be followed while the others cross. The label at the end of each line gives the current rank and the name, in place of a legend. Click a line or a label (on the keyboard, pick it with the up and down arrow keys and press Enter) to make that item the one in color, so any item's path can be followed the same way.

Rank 1 is at the top and periods are joined with S-curves. Labels ride on the right of the line ends and move with them, so the chart keeps room on the right for the longest label. The scrubber at the bottom is the time axis, so there is no separate period axis: the current period sits under its thumb, with the first and last periods at its ends.

When the card comes into view it waits on the first period, then moves on about every half second while the lines grow and the labels move up and down to that period's ranks, so each overtake is visible. It stops on the last period, and the still frame reads as an ordinary bump chart. Rewind, play/pause and fast-forward buttons sit to the right of the scrubber, under the label column. Play starts where the card stopped (from the start when at the end); rewind and fast-forward move one period per click, or keep moving at three times the playing speed while held and stop on the nearest period on release. Drag or click the scrubber, or press the left and right arrow keys, to move one period at a time. When the data changes and the card redraws, it draws the picked period at once.

Hover a line, or focus the chart and press the up and down arrow keys, to see that period's rank, value and move against the previous period while the other items fade. Playback pauses while the pointer is over the chart or the chart has keyboard focus.

range-slider.when: A control that picks a numeric range with two thumbs. Use it to filter a screen by a continuous value such as order value or quantity. Give it the distribution of the values and, while you drag, bars rise over the rail to show how much data falls in the range.
rules: Pick between `min` and `max` in steps of `step` (empty splits the range into about 100 steps). Give the first range in `value` as `[start, end]`; empty is the whole range. The picked values sit under the thumbs and move with them, by `format`; when they meet, they merge into one 'start – end'.

Give `counts`, the number of records in each equal-width bin from `min` to `max`, and while you drag or move a thumb with the keys, a distribution panel rises over the rail: the bars inside the range take the text color and the count inside the range is written with `noun` (rows when empty). Picking by the range alone hides where the data piles up, which makes it easy to filter it away; at rest only the rail and the values remain, so the slider takes little room in a filter bar. Matching `step` to the bin width makes the count exact.
Each time the value changes, the card sends a `vzb-change` event. `detail.name` is `name` and `detail.value` is `[start, end]` as numbers. The current value is also on the card as `data-vzb-value`.

Drag a thumb, press the rail to bring the nearer thumb there, or focus a thumb and press the arrow keys to move one step (Page Up and Down about ten steps, Home and End to the end). The thumbs follow like a spring; bars rise a little as they enter the range, nearest to the moving thumb first, and dip as they leave.

filter-chips.when: A control that picks several items from a fixed list as chips. Use it to filter a screen by a few names, such as channels or regions. The All chip at the front shows how many are picked.
rules: List the items in `options` and the first picks in `value` (empty picks all). Past two rows the chips go on one row that scrolls sideways, so about 8 items, all visible at a glance, fit best.

The All chip at the front (`all`; empty means "All", an empty string leaves it out) shows the number picked as a rolling number, and pressing it picks everything, or clears everything when all are picked. How many are on is always in view, so a filter is never left on by mistake.

Each time the value changes, the card sends a `vzb-change` event. `detail.name` is `name` and `detail.value` is the picked items in the order of `options`. The current value is also on the card as `data-vzb-value`.

A chip squashes a little when pressed and springs back, and when picked a check is drawn as the chip widens. Picked chips are filled with the text color so they do not compete with the data colors of the charts. Tab moves between chips and Space or Enter picks.

download-button.when: A button that downloads the data of a chart card on the screen as a file. It starts as an icon alone; hover and the formats to pick from (CSV, JSON, PNG) come out. Use it to export exactly what the controls show.
rules: Write the kind of the card to download in `target` (its `data-vzb`, e.g. `warning-bars`). The table comes from the current JSON of the first such card on the page: `items`, else `labels` with `values` (adding `limit` and `target` as columns when present), `labels` with `series`, else the first array of objects. It reads the JSON after the controls changed it, so you get what you see.

List the formats in `formats` (`csv`, `json`, `png`; empty means all three). The CSV starts with a BOM so Excel reads non-English text correctly, and the PNG is the card as you see it at twice the size (its text may be drawn in a font installed on the device). The file name is `filename` plus the extension of the format.

An icon alone takes little room on the screen; hover it, reach it with the keyboard or press it and the button widens and the formats come out one by one. Pressing the icon again while open downloads the first format, Esc closes it, and the left and right arrows move between the formats. The widened button floats over what is next to it instead of pushing it, and when there is no room on the right it opens to the left, keeping the icon in place. To put it at the right end, as at the top right of a screen, set `align` to `end`: the icon sits at the right end and the button opens to the left.

Before downloading, the card sends a `vzb-download` event (`detail: { name, target, format, filename, rows }`). If the page calls `preventDefault()` the card makes no file, so a screen that fetches the source data from a server can use the same button.

When the file is saved, the arrow drops into the tray and turns into a check, and the format and the number of rows (for a PNG, its size) roll up next to the button and fade after 1.8 s. When there is nothing to download, the button shakes and says "No data".
